text:
nina-sales: Heads up — CorpX is asking for a Private deployment POC. They want guidance on whether VPC peering or PrivateLink is better for their security posture and how that affects pricing. Can infra + solutions weigh in?
liam-eng: short answer: PrivateLink if they need one-way, managed endpoints and strict allowlists; peering if they want full VPC-level access. tradeoffs: PrivateLink avoids route table changes and is better for segmented security teams.
victor-netops: they also flagged internal firewall rules: only outbound to specific IP ranges allowed. if we go PrivateLink we can provide a set of endpoint IPs, but if Dedicated/reserved hosts are used we need to lock down egress ranges.
maggie-se: CorpX security questionnaire wants: SOC2 compliance, customer-managed KMS, audit logs for request payloads, and option for on-prem connector. Are we comfortable answering that for Private deployment POC?
liam-eng: we can confirm SOC2 and audit logs. customer-managed KMS is supported in Private with KMS integration, but for hosted Dedicated we'd need a separate enterprise plan — call that out in the quote.
sam-legal: note: encryption-at-rest + in-transit OK. but if they want payload-level access controls (e.g., redact PII before it leaves their network) we should be explicit about data flow and responsibilities.
nina-sales: timeline ask from CorpX: 2-week POC to validate connectivity and latency, then a pilot for 3 months. they want a cost estimate upfront (including egress, dedicated capacity delta, and potential connector engineering time).
maggie-se: for pricing: list two options in the quote — (A) PrivateLink + hosted nodes (lower setup ops, slightly higher egress) (B) Dedicated Private deployment in their VPC (higher monthly commit, predictable perf, includes reserved GPUs). include an engineering-hours line item for connector work.
victor-netops: firewall rules we need from them: allowed outbound CIDR(s) to our endpoints, allowed SNI if TLS-inspecting proxies are present, and any corporate proxy that will break mTLS. Example snippet we can give them:
```
# Allowlist example for PrivateLink
- Destination: 34.198.12.0/24  # endpoint pool (example)
- Ports: 443 (TCP)
- Protocol: TLS1.2+ (SNI required)
```
nina-sales: can someone produce the exact CIDRs and FQDNs we can provide in the next 24h? CorpX's security team needs them for their change window.
liam-eng: i'll generate a short export of current endpoint IP pools for the dedicated regions they requested (us-east-1 + eu-west-1). will include fallback ranges for burst/burst-gateway.
maggie-se: also confirm NAT/SNAT behavior: if they must preserve client IP downstream, PrivateLink + our edge NAT will rewrite source. for true src-IP preservation they'd need a dedicated on-prem connector or bring-your-own-proxy in front. that could affect their app telemetry.
victor-netops: clarify: PrivateLink keeps connections initiated from their VPC -> our endpoint; return traffic comes from our infra IPs. if they rely on source IP for allowlisting third-party services, call that out.
sam-legal: security questionnaire item 12 — data residency/stay-in-region: for Private deployment we can pin region; for Hosted with PrivateLink we can route to regional pool but need agreement in contract. add this to the POC SOW.
ops-bot: deployment-note: POC starter bundle requires 40 compute-hours reserved across 2 GPUs per region. request submitted (REQ-12345).
maggie-se: final ask for handoff doc: give customer a one-pager that lists (1) chosen connectivity pattern (peering vs PrivateLink) (2) exact firewall allowlist (CIDRs and ports) (3) expected behavior re: src-IP + NAT (4) pricing options and engineering estimate (5) SOW timeline.
nina-sales: i'll own the one-pager. liam, victor — please DM me the CIDRs and the short connectivity blurb so i can fold into the quote. Sam — can you draft the security answers for the questionnaire by EOD tomorrow?
sam-legal: yes — will take point, i'll flag any contractual needs (KMS, audit retention) in the draft.
liam-eng: sending the IP list now in DM :email: will include an example tcpdump and expected latency numbers for their path.
victor-netops: one potential blocker: CorpX uses TLS inspection with expired CA pinning. if their proxy intercepts TLS and re-signs, mutual TLS to our endpoints will fail. we should add a checklist for 'allow passthrough of our SNI or bypass for endpoint FQDNs'.
maggie-se: noted. i'll add that as a risk item in the one-pager. nina-sales — do we want to offer a short canary: 3-day connectivity validation before the 2-week POC? helps them unblock firewall change windows.
nina-sales: yes good idea. add it as option 0 in the quote. :thumbsup:
maggie-se: ok wrapping up — i'll draft the one-pager and attach the allowlist snippet + pricing options. expect a draft in ~6 hours.
ops-bot: reminder: engineering-hours budget counter updated: 8h allocated to this POC from Solutions (ticket SOL-789).
nina-sales: perfect — thanks everyone. i'll coordinate with CorpX and push the questionnaire deadline to EOD tomorrow per Sam.
liam-eng: SG. ping me if they need traceroutes or tcpdumps from their side.
maggie-se: :rocket:
